fun_facts: A swordfish keeps its brain and eyes running warm, up to 15°C above the near-freezing water it hunts in hundreds of feet down, using a heater organ built from modified eye muscle whose mass outweighs its own heart.
By the time a swordfish reaches adulthood it has no teeth and no scales at all, despite carrying the longest, heaviest bill of any billfish and being one of the ocean's more formidable predators.
Swordfish spend the day far deeper than a diver could survive, often 1,500 feet down or more in near-freezing water, then ride that same water column back up toward the surface every night to feed.

measures.label: Lower jaw fork length
measures.help: Tip of the lower jaw to the fork of the tail, measured in a straight line -- the standard billfish measurement, and the one federal minimum sizes are written in.

vocabs.label: Sex
vocabs.help: Swordfish cannot be sexed externally in the field; unknown is the normal answer.

vocabs.label: Condition at release
vocabs.help: Billfish tagging is normally done boat-side, leaving the fish in the water where possible.

not_taggable.reason: a fish in poor condition or bleeding is unlikely to survive release, so tagging it wastes the tag and the reward

must_release.reason: under the federal 47-inch (about 1,194 mm) lower jaw fork length minimum for recreationally-caught swordfish
